service.name: CLA Assistant
service.configuration: owner dashboard and linked Gist; this file is not read by the hosted service

claAssistantAllowlistPolicy.rationale: A machine account cannot hold copyright in a contribution and cannot execute a CLA, so the individual/employer/corporate routes are meaningless for it. Automated dependency bumps carry no copyrightable authorship. Exempting these accounts removes a gate that can never be satisfied; it is not a bypass of the human contribution gate. The runbook's prohibition on allowlists targets HUMAN contributors gaining an undocumented bypass.
constraints: Enumerate specific bot logins only; never a wildcard (no `*[bot]`, no `*`).
Never add a human contributor to this allowlist under any route.
Add a bot only if it opens pull requests whose commits it authors AND it cannot sign a CLA (review-only bots such as code-review assistants author no commits and need no entry).
Human-authored commits inside an otherwise-bot PR are not exempted; the CLA gate still applies to the human author.

entries.dependabot[bot]: GitHub Dependabot; automated dependency and GitHub Actions version bumps (.github/dependabot.yml).
entries.dependabot-preview[bot]: Legacy Dependabot identity; retained so a bump attributed to it is covered.

enforcement.maintainerOverrideScope: repository administrators may consciously bypass pull-request rules; this is not an automatic CLA exemption

privacy.proof: redacted schema only; no signature records
